mechanism_narrative: The observed accelerating decline in RETAIL_REC mobility over the past four weeks indicates a persistent trend of reduced public engagement that will continue to depress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A stabilization or slight reversal in the recent surge of residential mobility, indicating a potential 'stay-at-home fatigue', will trigger a modest rebound in retail and recreation activity as individuals seek limited outings over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 1 point week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues its decline even if RESIDENTIAL mobility stabilizes or slightly decreases.

mechanism_narrative: The concurrent and accelerating decline in both workplace attendance and public transit usage signifies a widespread reduction in daily commuting, which directly suppresses weekday retail and recreation footfall, leading to further declines over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an increase despite continued declines in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The widespread and accelerating decline in non-essential mobility categories (RETAIL_REC, WORKPLACES, TRANSIT) indicates an active period of tightening public health restrictions or strong advisories, which will continue to suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows an upward trend over the next 28 days despite the continuation of current mobility patterns in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS mobility experiences a sharp week-on-week increase, it will signal a renewed public willingness to engage in outdoor activities, potentially leading to a modest spillover effect into open-air retail and recreation over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 10 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline or remains flat even after a significant increase in PARKS mobility.

mechanism_narrative: The sustained and accelerating increase in residential mobility reflects a growing public preference for staying home, which will continue to directly suppress non-essential outings and drive down retail and recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL mobility remaining elevated or continuing to rise.

mechanism_narrative: The parallel and accelerating decline in both essential (GROCERY_PHARM) and non-essential (RETAIL_REC) mobility indicates a broad-based reduction in all out-of-home activities, signaling a deeper retrenchment that will further depress retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM continues to decline or remains low.

mechanism_narrative: A significant deceleration in the week-on-week decline of WORKPLACES mobility, signaling a potential stabilization of policy or a precursor to easing restrictions, will lead to a modest, delayed recovery in retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES decline rate slows by 50% week-on-week (e.g., from -6 to -3)
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline even if the rate of WORKPLACES decline significantly slows.
